outcome: Obstetric outcomes (cesarean section, stillbirths, prematurity, fetal growth restriction, postpartum hemorrhage)
cohort: 19,194 singleton births at 24 weeks of gestation and above in Qatar
finding: Compared to normotensive women, women with pre-eclampsia were older, more likely to be nulliparous, diabetic, and obese, and had an increased risk of preterm birth, cesarean deliveries, acute maternal morbidity, stillbirths, and low birth weight.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was more common in infants born to mothers with pre-eclampsia
